subject: VocaAI: tail latency surge for 32k long-window sessions - urgent
messages:
From: Jared Kim <jared.kim@voca.ai>
To: rishi_malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Cc: infra@voca.ai
Date: 2027-06-20T15:12:00Z
Subject: sudden p95/p99 spikes for our 32k sessions (started ~13:30 UTC)

Rishi,

We started seeing large p95/p99 spikes and intermittent 504s for our long-context inference (32k tokens) around 13:30 UTC today. Error rate climbed from ~0.1% to 3.4%, and a batch of production requests timed out. Attached is a small sample of failed request IDs and a trace PNG from our side.

Sample request id: voca-req-9a2f
Affected endpoints: /v1/generate (model: redwood-32k-v2)
Impact: UX freezes for users composing multi-document summaries. This is on an active paid plan (DEAL-4821). We need an ETA and temporary mitigation while you investigate—this is blocking a release tomorrow.

Can you confirm whether this is on your side or if we should roll back to 16k contexts?

Thanks,
Jared
Director of Platform
VocaAI
From: rishi_malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
To: laura_bennett <laura@redwood.ai>, dylan_brooks <dylan@redwood.ai>, hannah_schmitt <hannah@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: 
Date: 2027-06-20T15:18:00Z
Subject: Fwd: sudden p95/p99 spikes for our 32k sessions (started ~13:30 UTC)

Team — forwarding VocaAI. They’re seeing p95/p99 regressions and a small but impactful error spike on hosted for 32k windows. They ship tomorrow and need either a mitigation path or an ETA.

Quick asks:
- Dylan: can you triage kernel selection/batching changes in the last 8 hrs?
- Hannah: grab the per-model latency heatmap and the routing decisions for the affected times.
- Laura/Marissa: I might need an exec note if we need to offer credits or a temporary SLA concession.

I’ve attached their sample requests and the trace PNG they supplied.

—Rishi
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
From: dylan_brooks <dylan@redwood.ai>
To: rishi_malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura@redwood.ai>, hannah_schmitt <hannah@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-06-20T15:36:00Z
Subject: Re: Fwd: sudden p95/p99 spikes for our 32k sessions (started ~13:30 UTC)

I’m on it. Early look at the runtime logs shows an increase in slow paths for redwood-32k-v2 starting ~13:25 UTC correlated with a kernel policy change that was rolled to canary earlier this morning (optimize_kernel_v3). The change alters attention tiling heuristics and can push certain long-token sequences onto a fallback execution path that is slower and less batched.

Immediate steps I’m running:
- Replaying their sample requests against canary and stable to reproduce.
- Capturing the KV cache hit rates and batch sizes during the window.
- If can reproduce, rolling the kernel policy back for redwood-32k-v2 on the hosted fleet for region-us.

I’ll post updates in 30m.

—Dylan
SRE, Serving Runtime
From: hannah_schmitt <hannah@redwood.ai>
To: dylan_brooks <dylan@redwood.ai>, rishi_malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-06-20T15:45:00Z
Subject: Re: Fwd: sudden p95/p99 spikes for our 32k sessions (started ~13:30 UTC)

Attached: redwood-debug-log-8248.txt (selected traces), and a per-model latency heatmap for 06-20 12:00–16:00 UTC. Metrics show p95 for redwood-32k-v2 jumped from ~420ms to ~1.8s; p99 moved to ~3.6s. Error spike maps to our request timeout threshold.

Note: routing shows a bump in traffic routed to the canary pool for the model at 12:58 UTC due to autoscaling churn. That aligns with the kernel rollout Dylan mentioned.

Temporary mitigation we can offer customers immediately:
- Add a per-customer route policy to pin VocaAI to stable kernel profile (no canary) for redwood-32k-v2.
- Advise Voca to reduce max context to 16k while we fully validate kernel_v3 behavior (we can do a safe auto-fallback).

If Dylan can confirm a rollback, we can flip routing in ~10–15 minutes.

—Hannah
Incidents & Observability
From: dylan_brooks <dylan@redwood.ai>
To: rishi_malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura@redwood.ai>, hannah_schmitt <hannah@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-06-20T16:01:00Z
Subject: Re: Fwd: sudden p95/p99 spikes for our 32k sessions (started ~13:30 UTC)

Confirmed reproduction against canary using their sample corpus — the new tiling heuristic causes a subset of long sequences with repeating attention patterns to hit an unoptimized fallback. Rollback in progress for canary kernel policy targeting redwood-32k-v2 in us. Estimated time-to-roll: ~12 minutes.

I recommend we also apply a per-customer pin to stable while we monitor for 60m. Hannah, pls prepare a routing rule I can flip after rollback.

—Dylan
From: rishi_malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
To: Jared Kim <jared.kim@voca.ai>, infra@voca.ai
Cc: laura_bennett <laura@redwood.ai>, dylan_brooks <dylan@redwood.ai>, hannah_schmitt <hannah@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-06-20T16:20:00Z
Subject: RE: sudden p95/p99 spikes for our 32k sessions (started ~13:30 UTC)

Jared — quick update: we’ve identified a canary kernel policy rollout that caused some 32k workloads to fall back to a slower execution path. Dylan has rolled the canary change back for the US hosted fleet and Hannah is standing up a per-customer routing pin to keep Voca on the stable kernel profile while we monitor.

Temporary options if you need immediate relief on your side: (1) set max_context to 16k (safe, preserves throughput), or (2) enable a client-side short retry with exponential backoff so user-facing timeouts are less visible while we validate.

We plan to monitor for the next hour and will follow up with a short incident summary + remediation plan. If this impacts your release tomorrow and you need credits or a formal SLA exception, flag that here and I’ll escalate internally.

Apologies for the disruption — we know this is timing-sensitive.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Jared Kim <jared.kim@voca.ai>
To: rishi_malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, infra@voca.ai
Cc: procurement@voca.ai
Date: 2027-06-21T11:05:00Z
Subject: RE: sudden p95/p99 spikes for our 32k sessions (started ~13:30 UTC)

Thanks — appreciate the quick detection and rollback. We applied the 16k temp config and see p95 back to ~430ms and error rate normalized. We’d like the incident note and confirmation when the canary policy is fully validated before re-enabling 32k for Voca. Also please open a ticket for a post-mortem so our platform team can sync with yours.

We may request a credit depending on final SLA impact; Jared (procurement) is CC’d.

—Jared
Director of Platform, VocaAI
